items.title: Summit, Akeso tout biliary cancer win for PD-1/VEGF in China—but details are pending
items.snippet: The Phase 3 readout is the first for ivonescimab beyond non-small cell lung cancer to show a significant overall survival benefit, according to Summit Therapeutics and China-based partner Akeso.

items.title: BMS ends Cellares pact over cell therapy production problems, triggering layoffs
items.snippet: Setbacks to efforts to use Cellares’ automated platform to make an approved CAR-T cell therapy led BMS to terminate its partnership with the manufacturing specialist.

items.title: Biohaven could get up to $795M in epilepsy alliance with SK Bio
items.snippet: At the center of Biohaven’s agreement with SK Biopharmaceutical is the ion channel platform and the lead epilepsy candidate opakalim, for which Phase 2/3 data are expected later this year.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Jazz scores front-line gastric cancer nod from FDA for ‘practice-changing’ Ziihera
items.snippet: Gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma presents the biggest market opportunity for Jazz Pharmaceuticals’ Ziihera, according to Truist Securities, which forecasts peak sales of the drug to reach $2.5 billion.

items.title: FDA eyes 2 new deputy commissioner posts: Report
items.snippet: Though the potential change is unconfirmed, media outlets reported Wednesday that one deputy commissioner would focus on the intersection between health and AI, while another will be dedicated to drugs.

items.title: Capricor’s DMD therapy still alive, Merck/Moderna’s cancer vax shines, FDA’s future revealed
items.snippet: FDA extends its review of Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy as an unhappy shareholder advocates for change; Merck and Moderna tout positive data for their mRNA-based cancer vaccine; Trump nominates White House aide Heidi Overton as FDA commissioner; and the oral obesity market heats up wi...

items.title: CDMO hiring tough as demand for specialized talent outpaces supply
items.snippet: The talent pool not keeping pace with increased outsourcing demand is just one reason CDMOs have trouble filling roles, according to a search expert. He also told BioSpace who is most in demand and how candidates can stand out from the competition.

items.title: Inside the Gulf biotech deal model, ahead of RGMBS 2026 in Riyadh
items.snippet: Sovereign capital, guaranteed offtake, and localization mandates are reshaping how biotech deals get structured in the Gulf, ahead of the Riyadh Global Medical Biotechnology Summit (RGMBS) 2026, 14 to 16 September, where 59 agreements have been signed across three editions.

items.title: Biotech IPOs approach ‘escape velocity’ barring yellow flags that could threaten rebound
items.snippet: Twenty-five biotechs have used the IPO route to go public this year—with five of those debuts occurring this month alone. It’s the most IPOs since 2021, when the industry recorded 78 during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: Cellares cuts jobs after losing pharma customer
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: China’s Haisco forms immunology biotech with up to $1.5B from American VCs
items.snippet: Haisco Pharmaceutical Group has been on a deal hot streak this year, inking major deals with Eli Lilly, AbbVie and more. The new company will take on one of Haisco’s core immunology assets.

items.title: Bausch + Lomb advances dry eye disease drug to Phase 3 despite mid-stage fail
items.snippet: While Bausch + Lomb’s dual-action eye drops failed to outperform active comparators at day 29, the investigational asset showed significant superiority at day 15.

items.title: Lilly takes oral obesity race abroad with UK launch of Foundayo
items.snippet: Eli Lilly’s best play for Foundayo is to bring it overseas, a more price-sensitive market where the pharma can more readily outcompete Novo Nordisk “given the high margins of a small-molecule therapy,” Truist analyst Srikripa Devarakonda told BioSpace.

items.title: Massachusetts biopharma jobs, including R&D positions, fell in 2025: Report
items.snippet: After barely growing in 2024, biopharma employment in Massachusetts dropped 3.1% last year. R&D jobs dipped even more, by 3.9%. Biomanufacturing, however, went up.

items.title: Preparing for Novartis showdown, Curium touts value of radiopharma supply resiliency
items.snippet: While Novartis’ Pluvicto is a blockbuster, Curium heads into talks with the FDA about the review of its rival drug candidate believing a competing product can make the supply chain more resilient.

items.title: Capricor’s Duchenne therapy has new life after FDA grants 3-month extension
items.snippet: The FDA has granted a three-month extension for Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy hopeful deramiocel in order to review additional data and consider a refined indication. The new target action date for the therapy is November 22.

items.title: REGENXBIO’s Hunter syndrome gene therapy hit by FDA hold, stymieing resubmission plans
items.snippet: The FDA has placed a clinical hold on RGX-121 after small nodules or cystic masses were detected in the spines of five patients enrolled in REGENXBIO’s registrational trial. The biotech no longer plans to resubmit the candidate—which was rejected in February—in the near term.

items.title: Roche bets up to $2.3B in Hanmi pact for next-gen weight loss drug
items.snippet: Roche, through its subsidiary Genentech, will gain access to the investigational asset HM17321, which is designed to not only elicit weight loss but also improve lean mass.

items.title: Kennedy questions vaccination guidelines following Trump’s order to break up MMR
items.snippet: The current classifications of vaccine recommendations could imply that not all shots require the consent of patients or their parents, according to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

items.title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
items.snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

items.title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
items.snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
